title: LinkMe File Uploads Can Use CDP Injection When Picker Is Blocked
summary: Codex in-app browser blocks ordinary LinkMe file picker automation, but ATLAS can prepare upload-safe assets and inject user-approved files into the correct hidden LinkMe input through CDP Runtime.evaluate.

metadata.source: live Codex desktop LinkMe setup session

context.goal: Upload custom gothic green/black brand icons to LinkMe featured cards.

metadata.decision: When Codex in-app browser blocks ordinary LinkMe file picker automation, prepare upload-safe assets in ATLAS, then inject a File object into the correct hidden LinkMe file input through the tab CDP runtime and dispatch input/change events. Confirm the LinkMe Use Image dialog, click Use Original or Crop Image, then click Update and verify the public page visually.
evidence: Codex in-app browser reported that file uploads are not supported by Codex in-app browser.
Clicking LinkMe's Upload an icon control did not surface a native Windows Open dialog in the window list.
LinkMe exposes hidden file inputs, and direct DOM.setFileInputFiles is blocked in the in-app browser.
CDP Runtime.evaluate can create a browser File object from an ATLAS-prepared base64 asset, assign it to the correct hidden input via DataTransfer, and dispatch input/change events.
On 2026-07-08 this successfully uploaded the workout and Discord green/black gothic assets to the public LinkMe page.

metadata.workflow_rule: For future Codex LinkMe customization: save and compress user-provided assets into tmp/linkme-icons, inspect current file input order because it changes by card state, target the hidden input whose parentText matches the intended control, inject through CDP Runtime.evaluate, confirm the image dialog, save, then verify the public LinkMe page with a screenshot.
metadata.recommended_execution_path: Codex prepares assets, uses CDP Runtime.evaluate only for the user-approved LinkMe asset upload, saves the card, and verifies public visual state. Fall back to manual upload only if the page no longer accepts synthetic input/change events.
